topic: Named in a cyber case? Arrest isn't automatic — the 7-year line: most IT Act offences carry up to 3 years and are bailable (s.77B; SC, Jul 2026), BNS cheating s.318(4) added to cyber FIRs carries up to 7 years and is non-bailable; for offences up to 7 years a BNSS s.35(3) notice is the rule and arrest the exception, with reasons in writing (Satender Kumar Antil, SC, 15 Jan 2026); the notice must be obeyed and served physically, not on WhatsApp (SC, Jul 2025); IT Act offences investigated by an Inspector or above (s.78); seized phone: seizure list, video-recorded seizure (BNSS s.105), hash value (BSA s.63, EP09); a video-call 'arrest' is always a scam (I4C); one-minute check: save 1930
audience: Everyday users, young people, shopkeepers and employees who could be named in a cyber complaint (primary); law students
